statements.label: supported
statements.text: Rosaceae were dated to a Late Cretaceous origin, with rapid bursts of diversification occurring in several geological periods.
statements.evidence: Rosaceae were estimated to have originated during the Late Cretaceous with evidence for rapid diversification events during several geological periods.
statements.note: The abstract dates the family's origin to the Late Cretaceous and reports rapid diversification events in several periods.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Rosaceae genera that radiated from the early Oligocene onward did so in colder and drier environments than the warm, wet habitats where major lineages diversified in the Late Cretaceous.
statements.evidence: The major lineages rapidly diversified in warm and wet habits during the Late Cretaceous, and the rapid diversification of genera from the early Oligocene onwards occurred in colder and drier environments.
statements.note: The abstract contrasts the warm, wet setting of Late Cretaceous lineage radiation with the colder, drier setting of genus radiation from the early Oligocene.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Apomictic Rosaceae genera were found to have diversified faster than sexually reproducing Rosaceae genera.
statements.evidence: Phylogenetic relationships in Rosaceae have long been problematic because of frequent hybridisation, apomixis and presumed rapid radiation
statements.note: Apomixis appears only as a background reason why the phylogeny was hard to resolve; the abstract compares no diversification rates between reproductive modes.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The plastome analyses recovered three subfamilies and 16 tribes of Rosaceae, as previously delimited, as strongly supported monophyletic groups.
statements.evidence: Three subfamilies and 16 tribes (as previously delimited) were strongly supported as monophyletic
statements.note: The abstract states that three subfamilies and 16 previously delimited tribes received strong support as monophyletic.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: The study dated the switch from carnivory to pollen feeding in the bee lineage to the Cretaceous.
statements.evidence: Establishing the phylogenetic affinities of ants and bees helps us understand and reconstruct patterns of social evolution as well as fully appreciate the biological implications of the switch from carnivory to pollen feeding (pollenivory).
statements.note: The carnivory-to-pollenivory switch is mentioned only as motivation, and the abstract reports no divergence dates of any kind.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The study showed that taxon choice has a fundamental effect on tree topology and clade support in phylogenomic inference.
statements.evidence: We also demonstrate that taxon choice can fundamentally impact tree topology and clade support in phylogenomic inference.
statements.note: The abstract explicitly reports a demonstration that taxon choice affects both topology and clade support.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The UCE dataset comprised more than 800 loci from 187 samples, representing 30 of the 31 aculeate families.
statements.evidence: gathering sequence data from >800 UCE loci and 187 samples, including 30 out of 31 aculeate families
statements.note: The abstract gives the dataset as >800 UCE loci and 187 samples covering 30 of 31 aculeate families.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Ants were recovered as the sister group of Apoidea (bees plus apoid wasps), with bees nested inside a paraphyletic Crabronidae.
statements.evidence: we find unequivocal evidence that ants are the sister group to bees+apoid wasps (Apoidea) and that bees are nested within a paraphyletic Crabronidae
statements.note: The abstract reports unequivocal evidence for both the ant-Apoidea sister relationship and bees nesting within a paraphyletic Crabronidae.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Compared with other archaea, Asgard archaea experienced significantly more gene duplication events and fewer gene loss events during genome evolution.
statements.evidence: genome evolution in Asgard archaea involved significantly more gene duplication and fewer gene loss events compared with other archaea
statements.note: The reconciliation analyses showed significantly more duplications and fewer losses in Asgard archaea than in other archaea.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Eukaryotes formed a well-nested clade inside Asgard archaea, branching as the sister lineage of Hodarchaeales, a newly proposed order within Heimdallarchaeia.
statements.evidence: We find that eukaryotes are placed, with high confidence, as a well-nested clade within Asgard archaea and as a sister lineage to Hodarchaeales, a newly proposed order within Heimdallarchaeia.
statements.note: The abstract places eukaryotes with high confidence within Asgard archaea as the sister lineage of Hodarchaeales.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The study inferred that the last common ancestor of Asgard archaea was a thermophilic chemolithotroph, while the lineage leading to eukaryotes adapted to mesophilic conditions.
statements.evidence: we infer that the last common ancestor of Asgard archaea was probably a thermophilic chemolithotroph and that the lineage from which eukaryotes evolved adapted to mesophilic conditions
statements.note: The abstract infers a thermophilic chemolithotrophic Asgard ancestor and a shift to mesophily in the lineage that gave rise to eukaryotes.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: The study showed that eukaryotic cellular complexity emerged before the eukaryotic lineage acquired mitochondria.
statements.evidence: Our work provides key insights into the prokaryote-to-eukaryote transition and a platform for better understanding the emergence of cellular complexity in eukaryotic cells.
statements.note: The abstract offers a platform for studying how cellular complexity emerged but reports nothing about mitochondria or the timing of their acquisition.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The Columbian mammoth of North America descends from a Middle Pleistocene hybridization between two mammoth lineages, each contributing roughly half of its ancestry.
statements.evidence: the Columbian mammoth of North America traces its ancestry to a Middle Pleistocene hybridization between these two lineages, with roughly equal admixture proportions
statements.note: The abstract reports a Middle Pleistocene hybrid origin of the Columbian mammoth with roughly equal admixture from the two lineages.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: The previously unrecognized mammoth lineage was found to have died out in Siberia after giving rise to the first North American mammoths.
statements.evidence: One of these lineages gave rise to the woolly mammoth and the other represents a previously unrecognized lineage that was ancestral to the first mammoths to colonize North America.
statements.note: The abstract identifies what this lineage gave rise to but says nothing about whether or when it disappeared from Siberia.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Of the three Early and Middle Pleistocene mammoth specimens that yielded genome-wide data, two are older than one million years.
statements.evidence: three mammoth specimens dating to the Early and Middle Pleistocene subepochs, two of which are more than one million years old
statements.note: The abstract states that two of the three sequenced specimens exceed one million years in age.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Most of the protein-coding changes linked to cold adaptation in woolly mammoths had already arisen by one million years ago.
statements.evidence: the majority of protein-coding changes associated with cold adaptation in woolly mammoths were already present one million years ago
statements.note: The abstract reports that the majority of cold-adaptation coding changes were already present a million years ago.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Innate immunity genes as a group have been shaped by stronger purifying selection than the rest of the protein-coding genes.
statements.evidence: innate immunity genes have globally evolved under stronger purifying selection than the remainder of protein-coding genes
statements.note: The abstract directly compares purifying selection on innate immunity genes with that on other protein-coding genes and finds it stronger.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: A scan for local adaptation detected 57 high-scoring positive selection signals at innate immunity genes.
statements.evidence: detect 57 high-scoring signals of positive selection at innate immunity genes
statements.note: The abstract gives the count of 57 high-scoring positive selection signals at innate immunity genes.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: The study tied the recent adaptations at innate immunity genes to the spread of specific epidemic pathogens such as smallpox.
statements.evidence: Furthermore, we show that most adaptations targeting coding variation have occurred in the last 6,000-13,000 years, the period at which populations shifted from hunting and gathering to farming.
statements.note: The abstract links the timing of these adaptations to the transition to farming but names no specific pathogen as their driver.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Compared with the remainder of the coding genome, innate immunity genes carry higher levels of Neandertal introgression.
statements.evidence: innate immunity genes present higher Neandertal introgression than the remainder of the coding genome
statements.note: The abstract reports higher Neandertal introgression in innate immunity genes than in the rest of the coding genome.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: X-bearing spermatids were found to express more genes than Y-bearing spermatids.
statements.evidence: Further work identified transcriptomal differences between X- and Y-bearing spermatids
statements.note: The abstract reports that X- and Y-bearing spermatids differ transcriptionally but does not say which of them expresses more genes.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The single-nucleus transcriptome analysis covered testes from 11 species, spanning eutherians, marsupials, monotremes and birds, and including seven primates.
statements.evidence: single-nucleus transcriptome data for testes from 11 species that cover the three main mammalian lineages (eutherians, marsupials and monotremes) and birds (the evolutionary outgroup), and include seven primates
statements.note: The abstract describes testis data from 11 species across the three main mammalian lineages and birds, seven of them primates.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Rapid testis evolution was driven by accelerated fixation of gene expression changes, amino acid substitutions and new genes in late spermatogenic stages.
statements.evidence: the rapid evolution of the testis was driven by accelerated fixation rates of gene expression changes, amino acid substitutions and new genes in late spermatogenic stages
statements.note: The abstract attributes rapid testis evolution to accelerated fixation rates of these three kinds of change in late spermatogenic stages.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: X chromosomes became enriched during evolution for genes that are predominantly expressed in spermatogonia and Sertoli cells.
statements.evidence: Genes predominantly expressed in spermatogonia (germ cells fuelling spermatogenesis) and Sertoli (somatic support) cells accumulated on X chromosomes during evolution
statements.note: The abstract reports that spermatogonia- and Sertoli-biased genes accumulated on X chromosomes over evolution.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Teleost lineages with higher MHC I copy numbers showed higher speciation rates under trait-dependent diversification models.
statements.evidence: we identify an association between high MHC I copy number and elevated speciation rates using trait-dependent diversification models
statements.note: The abstract reports an association between high MHC I copy number and elevated speciation rates from trait-dependent models.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: MHC I genes expanded on several independent occasions, both within Gadiformes and in teleost lineages outside that clade.
statements.evidence: In contrast, we find that MHC I gene expansions have occurred multiple times, both inside and outside this clade.
statements.note: The abstract states that MHC I expansions occurred multiple times, inside and outside Gadiformes.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Genome sequencing of 66 teleost species showed that MHC II is absent throughout Gadiformes, indicating a single loss in their common ancestor.
statements.evidence: for 66 teleost species, we show here that MHC II is missing in the entire Gadiformes lineage and thus was lost once in their common ancestor
statements.note: The abstract reports MHC II missing across the whole Gadiformes lineage from analyses of 66 species, implying one ancestral loss.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Gadiformes species lacking MHC II were found to suffer more bacterial infections than other teleosts.
statements.evidence: The genomic basis of a particularly aberrant strategy is exemplified by Atlantic cod, in which a loss of major histocompatibility complex (MHC) II functionality coincides with a marked expansion of MHC I genes.
statements.note: The abstract characterises MHC II loss only at the genomic level and reports no measure of infection rates or disease susceptibility.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Non-nodulating relatives of Parasponia showed parallel, independent losses of putative orthologs of NIN, RPG and NOD FACTOR PERCEPTION.
statements.evidence: show evidence of parallel loss in nonnodulating species of putative orthologs of NIN , RPG , and NOD FACTOR PERCEPTION
statements.note: The comparative genome analysis found parallel loss of these putative symbiosis-gene orthologs in nonnodulating species.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Introducing NIN and RPG into Trema tomentosa was shown to enable it to form nitrogen-fixing nodules.
statements.evidence: This will have profound implications for translational approaches aimed at engineering nitrogen-fixing nodules in crop plants.
statements.note: The abstract mentions nodule engineering only as a future implication and reports no gene-transfer experiment in Trema.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Nodules of Parasponia andersonii and the legume Medicago truncatula draw on at least 290 shared orthologous symbiosis genes.
statements.evidence: Comparative transcriptomics of P. andersonii and the legume Medicago truncatula revealed utilization of at least 290 orthologous symbiosis genes in nodules.
statements.note: The comparative transcriptomics result gives a minimum of 290 orthologous symbiosis genes used in nodules of both species.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Crosses between Parasponia andersonii and non-nodulating Trema tomentosa showed that nodule organogenesis is genetically dominant, whereas intracellular infection is not.
statements.evidence: Intergeneric crosses between Parasponia andersonii and its nonnodulating relative Trema tomentosa demonstrated that nodule organogenesis, but not intracellular infection, is a dominant genetic trait.
statements.note: The intergeneric crosses showed dominance for nodule organogenesis but explicitly not for intracellular infection.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Most of the para- or polyphyletic butterfly groups identified by the study belong to the brush-footed butterflies (Nymphalidae).
statements.evidence: This study overturns prior notions of the taxon's evolutionary history, as many long-recognized subfamilies and tribes are para- or polyphyletic.
statements.note: The abstract says many subfamilies and tribes are non-monophyletic but does not say which families they fall in.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Butterflies arose about 119 million years ago, yet most living lineages diverged later, after the K-Pg mass extinction 65 million years ago.
statements.evidence: Butterflies originated around 119 million years ago (mya) in the late Cretaceous, but most extant lineages diverged after the Cretaceous-Paleogene (K-Pg) mass-extinction 65 mya.
statements.note: The dated phylogeny puts the butterfly origin at about 119 mya and most extant lineage splits after the K-Pg event 65 mya.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Association with ants arose independently three times in butterflies: once in Lycaenidae and twice in Riodinidae.
statements.evidence: Ant association independently evolved once in Lycaenidae and twice in Riodinidae.
statements.note: The abstract counts one independent origin of ant association in Lycaenidae and two in Riodinidae.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Nocturnal Hedylidae grouped with skippers inside the butterfly tree, indicating a secondary reversal from diurnal to nocturnal activity.
statements.evidence: followed by skippers (Hesperiidae) + the nocturnal butterflies (Hedylidae) as sister to the remainder, indicating a secondary reversal from diurnality to nocturnality
statements.note: The placement of Hedylidae with skippers is stated to indicate a secondary reversal from diurnality to nocturnality.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The study attributed the link between effective population size and adaptive substitution mainly to a lower nearly-neutral substitution rate under more efficient purifying selection in large populations.
statements.evidence: This relationship, however, appears to be primarily driven by a decreased rate of nearly-neutral amino-acid substitution because of more efficient purifying selection in large populations.
statements.note: The abstract traces the correlation primarily to a decreased nearly-neutral substitution rate caused by more efficient purifying selection in large populations.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: In a homogeneous dataset of 44 non-model animal species pairs, adaptive evolution contributed heavily to amino-acid substitution across all major metazoan phyla, with humans and primates the notable exception.
statements.evidence: homogeneous data set of 44 non-model animal species pairs. Data analysis uncovers a major contribution of adaptive evolution to the amino-acid substitution process across all major metazoan phyla-with the notable exception of humans and primates.
statements.note: Analysis of the 44 species pairs revealed a major adaptive contribution across metazoan phyla, except in humans and primates.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Adaptive amino-acid substitutions were found to be concentrated in immune-related genes across the animal species studied.
statements.evidence: Our results reveal that adaptive processes dominate the evolution of proteins in most animal species
statements.note: The abstract reports genome-wide adaptive rates only and does not break them down by gene function.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Species with larger effective population sizes showed a higher proportion of adaptive amino-acid substitutions.
statements.evidence: The proportion of adaptive amino-acid substitution is found to be positively correlated to species effective population size.
statements.note: A positive correlation means the adaptive proportion rises with effective population size, as the abstract states.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Adaptive convergence between the giant panda and the red panda was detected in the limb development genes DYNC2H1 and PCNT.
statements.evidence: Limb development genes DYNC2H1 and PCNT have undergone adaptive convergence
statements.note: The abstract names DYNC2H1 and PCNT as limb development genes that underwent adaptive convergence.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: The genes that converged in giant and red pandas were also found to have converged in other bamboo-eating mammals such as bamboo lemurs.
statements.evidence: These findings offer insights into genetic convergence mechanisms underlying phenotypic convergence and adaptation to a specialized bamboo diet.
statements.note: Only the two pandas were analysed; the abstract makes no claim about any other bamboo-eating mammal.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Both the giant panda and the red panda have lost a functional umami taste receptor gene, TAS1R1, which is now a pseudogene in each.
statements.evidence: the umami taste receptor gene TAS1R1 has been pseudogenized in both pandas
statements.note: The abstract states that TAS1R1 has been pseudogenized, that is, rendered non-functional, in both pandas.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Genes for digesting and using bamboo nutrients, including essential amino acids, fatty acids and vitamins, show adaptive convergence in the two pandas.
statements.evidence: adaptive convergence has occurred in genes involved in the digestion and utilization of bamboo nutrients such as essential amino acids, fatty acids, and vitamins
statements.note: The abstract reports adaptive convergence in genes for digesting and utilising these bamboo nutrients.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Larger bacterial genomes and higher rates of gene transfer are associated with a stronger concentration of transferred genes in hotspots.
statements.evidence: This concentration increases with genome size and with the rate of transfer.
statements.note: The abstract states that the concentration of transferred genes increases with both genome size and transfer rate.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Across 80 bacterial species, horizontally transferred genes cluster in hotspots that make up only about 1% of chromosomal regions.
statements.evidence: transferred genes are concentrated in only ~1% of the chromosomal regions (hotspots) in 80 bacterial species
statements.note: The abstract reports transferred genes concentrated in about 1% of chromosomal regions across 80 species.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Among naturally transformable bacteria, hotspots that carry fewer mobile genetic elements are overrepresented.
statements.evidence: Overrepresentation of hotspots with fewer mobile genetic elements in naturally transformable bacteria
statements.note: The abstract reports an overrepresentation of hotspots with fewer mobile genetic elements in naturally transformable bacteria.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Hotspots in pathogenic bacteria were found to hold more antibiotic resistance genes than hotspots in non-pathogenic bacteria.
statements.evidence: Most mobile genetic elements and antibiotic resistance genes are in hotspots
statements.note: The abstract places most resistance genes in hotspots but never compares pathogenic with non-pathogenic species.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: The study found that non-coding sequences evolve at more uniform rates across bird lineages than coding exons do.
statements.evidence: We suggest that the observed differences in the estimates of topology for these studies reflect data-type effects due to violations of the models used in phylogenetic analyses
statements.note: The abstract blames model violations linked to data type but does not identify rate uniformity, or any specific sequence property, as the difference.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The study assembled a new data matrix from 235 bird species in which non-coding sequences made up 90% of the data.
statements.evidence: a novel, large-scale data matrix comprising 90% non-coding sequences from 235 bird species
statements.note: The abstract describes the new matrix as 90% non-coding sequence from 235 bird species.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Adding more taxa to analyses of the new matrix increased congruence with the earlier taxon-poor, mostly non-coding tree, not the coding-dominated taxon-rich tree.
statements.evidence: increased taxon sampling actually resulted in increased congruence with the tree from the previous taxon-poor study (which had a majority of non-coding data) instead of the taxon-rich study (which largely used coding data)
statements.note: The abstract reports that more taxa moved the results towards the taxon-poor, non-coding-based tree rather than the taxon-rich one.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Although more taxa seemed to benefit the analyses, data type was the variable with the greatest influence on the Neoaves phylogenetic results.
statements.evidence: Although increased taxon sampling appeared to have a positive impact on phylogenetic analyses the most important variable was data type.
statements.note: The abstract names data type, not taxon sampling, as the most important variable.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: In contrast to earlier studies, the analyses placed the root of the archaeal tree between DPANN and all remaining Archaea.
statements.evidence: in contrast to previous work, place the tree root between DPANN and all other Archaea
statements.note: The abstract explicitly places the root between DPANN and all other Archaea, contrary to previous work.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The rooting model drew on gene duplications, horizontal transfers and gene losses recorded across 31,236 archaeal gene families.
statements.evidence: This model uses evidence from gene duplications, horizontal transfers, and gene losses contained in 31,236 archaeal gene families to identify the most likely root for the tree.
statements.note: The abstract states that the rooting model used duplication, transfer and loss events from 31,236 gene families.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Metabolic reconstruction on the rooted tree showed that early Archaea were thermophiles.
statements.evidence: Metabolic reconstructions on the rooted tree suggest that early Archaea were anaerobes that may have had the ability to reduce CO 2 to acetate via the Wood-Ljungdahl pathway.
statements.note: The reconstruction describes early Archaea as anaerobes possibly using the Wood-Ljungdahl pathway and says nothing about their temperature preference.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Contrary to the view that genome reduction dominated archaeal evolution, the inferred ancestor had a relatively small genome whose complexity later increased through gene duplication and horizontal transfer.
statements.evidence: In contrast to proposals suggesting that genome reduction has been the predominant mode of archaeal evolution, our analyses infer a relatively small-genomed archaeal ancestor that subsequently increased in complexity via gene duplication and horizontal gene transfer.
statements.note: The abstract infers a small-genomed ancestor that grew in complexity, explicitly contrasting this with genome-reduction proposals.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: As the phylogenomic datasets grew larger, the uncertainty attached to estimated diversification times shrank steadily.
statements.evidence: We show that increasingly larger phylogenomic datasets produce diversification time estimates with progressively smaller uncertainties
statements.note: The abstract reports that larger datasets gave diversification time estimates with progressively smaller uncertainties.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Applying the same Bayesian dating approach to flowering plants placed the origin of crown angiosperms in the Jurassic.
statements.evidence: This approach can be used to address other contentious cases of animal and plant diversifications that require analysis of species-level phylogenomic datasets.
statements.note: Plants are mentioned only as a possible future application; the abstract reports no plant analysis.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: A timetree covering 4,705 mammal species was estimated by integrating information from 72 mammal genomes.
statements.evidence: a Bayesian molecular-clock dating approach to estimate a timetree of 4,705 mammal species integrating information from 72 mammal genomes
statements.note: The abstract gives the timetree size as 4,705 species, built with information from 72 genomes.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Crown Placentalia were dated to the Late Cretaceous, and an explosive Palaeogene model of placental origination was confidently rejected.
statements.evidence: we confidently reject an explosive model of placental mammal origination in the Palaeogene 8 and show that crown Placentalia originated in the Late Cretaceous
statements.note: The abstract both rejects the explosive Palaeogene model and dates crown Placentalia to the Late Cretaceous.
